expectations.text: ADR has all required sections: Status, Context, Decision, Rationale, Consequences
expectations.evidence: No standalone 'Rationale' section. The ADR has Status, Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives Considered, Migration Plan, References — the rationale is embedded in Decision and Alternatives sections rather than as an explicit section header.
No AI Context section present. The ADR ends with a References section including an internal post-mortem link but no structured guidance for AI agents.

expectations.text: Context mentions the BullMQ/Redis failover problem specifically
expectations.evidence: Lines 13-16 describe 'jobs dequeued by workers but not yet committed to a persistent store are lost' during failover, and references INC-0047 post-mortem.

expectations.text: Rationale explains why Temporal was chosen over alternatives
expectations.evidence: Alternatives Considered section (lines 66-83) explains rejection of each alternative with specific reasons.

expectations.text: Consequences explicitly mentions the separate worker process and ops overhead
expectations.evidence: Line 57: 'Temporal workers are typically run as separate processes. This adds a deployment artifact and requires updates to CI/CD pipelines, health checks, and monitoring.'

expectations.text: AI Context section instructs an agent not to suggest reverting to BullMQ without reading the failover incident
expectations.evidence: No AI Context section. No explicit guidance for AI agents. The closest is a reference to 'Internal post-mortem: Redis failover incident (reference: INC-0047)' in References, but no agent-targeted instructions.
